events.title: .NET Framework 1.0 released
events.summary: On January 15, 2002, Microsoft shipped .NET Framework 1.0 — a unified platform for building Windows desktop and web apps with automatic memory management.
events.about: .NET Framework is Microsoft's managed runtime: write in C# or VB.NET, get garbage collection, shared libraries, web tools (ASP.NET), and database access in one stack. It powered enterprise Windows apps, internal portals, and desktop software for two decades until cross-platform .NET replaced it for new projects.

narrative.whyChosen: .NET Framework defined Microsoft's development stack for Windows desktop and web for twenty years.
narrative.whyImportant: It let C#, VB.NET, and other languages share one runtime and library ecosystem instead of fragmented Windows APIs.
narrative.problemSolved: Windows developers juggled incompatible APIs for desktop (COM/MFC) and web (classic ASP); .NET offered one managed platform for both.
